steps.title: Wash the work area first
steps.instruction: Wash and dry the bike before you open anything, paying extra attention to the area you are about to work on. Grit that falls into an open bearing bore or brake system is how good parts fail early. Have a clean tray and zip bags with a marker ready for fasteners.
verification: Work area is free of mud and grit
Parts tray and labelled bags are ready

steps.title: Put the bike on the lift stand
steps.instruction: Pull the plug-in stand out of the rear axle and lift the bike onto a lift stand, placing it under the frame below the engine. Both wheels should hang free. Rock the bike gently to make sure it sits square and cannot tip, and keep anyone off it while it is up.
verification: Both wheels are off the ground
Bike is stable when pushed lightly from each side

steps.title: Feel for play before you strip it
steps.instruction: Grab the swingarm at the back and try to move it up and down, then side to side. Clunks or side movement point at the pivot bearings; notchy or sticky movement through the stroke points at the linkage. Note what you feel so you can compare once it is rebuilt.
verification: Any play or roughness has been noted

steps.title: Take off the frame protectors
steps.instruction: Snip the cable ties, then remove the small screws and their bushings that hold the frame protectors. Lift the left protector away; slide the right one forward and drop it out from underneath. Bag the screws and bushings together.
verification: Both frame protectors are off
Screws and bushings are bagged

steps.title: Push the rear caliper piston back
steps.instruction: Squeeze the rear caliper toward the disc by hand to push the piston back a little; this gives the pads clearance so the wheel comes out and goes back in easily. Keep the caliper away from the spokes while you push.
verification: Pads are no longer dragging hard on the disc

steps.title: Remove the rear axle nut and adjuster
steps.instruction: Spin off the rear axle nut and lift off that side's chain adjuster block. Slide the axle out only part of the way, just enough that the wheel can roll forward in the swingarm.
verification: Nut and adjuster are bagged together
Axle is still holding the wheel

steps.title: Roll the wheel forward and lift the chain off
steps.instruction: Push the wheel as far forward as it will go to create slack, then lift the chain off the rear sprocket and lay it over a rag on the swingarm so it does not scratch anything.
verification: Chain is off the rear sprocket

steps.title: Pull the axle and lift the wheel out
steps.instruction: Hold the wheel up with one hand, pull the axle out, and lower the wheel out of the swingarm. Set it down on blocks or on its side with the brake disc facing up so the disc cannot be bent or contaminated. Take the two spacers out of the hub seals and keep them with the axle. From here on, do not touch the rear brake pedal.
verification: Wheel is out and resting so the disc carries no load
Both hub spacers are accounted for
Rear brake pedal has not been pressed

steps.title: Free the rear brake line and hang the caliper
steps.instruction: Unclip the rear brake hose from its guide on the swingarm. Slide the caliper forward off its mounting rail and hang it from the frame with a zip tie or wire so the hose is not stretched or kinked. The brake system stays closed; just keep your foot off the pedal.
verification: Caliper is hanging on a tie, not on its hose
Hose is free of the swingarm guide

steps.title: Split the chain at the master link
steps.instruction: Roll the chain until the master link is somewhere easy to reach, pop the spring clip off with pliers, remove the side plate and push the link out. Take the chain off and lay it on clean cardboard. Look at the clip: if it is bent or loose on the pins, plan on a new connecting link.
verification: Chain is off the bike
Master link parts are bagged
Clip condition noted

steps.title: Block the swingarm up
steps.instruction: Slide a wooden block or a small jack under the swingarm and lift it just enough to take the load off the linkage bolts. This keeps the bolts from binding as you pull them.
verification: Swingarm is supported
Linkage bolts are not under load

steps.title: Remove the lower shock bolt
steps.instruction: Remove the M10 bolt that holds the bottom of the shock to the angle lever. If it binds, raise or lower the swingarm block slightly until it slides out. Bag it on its own; it goes back with fresh thread locker.
verification: Shock eye is free of the angle lever
Bolt is bagged and labelled

steps.title: Disconnect the pull rod from the angle lever
steps.instruction: Remove the nut and bolt joining the pull rod (linkage lever) to the angle lever. Look at the bolt head before it comes out: it has a flat that locks against the part beside it, and it must go back the same way. Snap a photo.
verification: Pull rod is free of the angle lever
Photo taken of the bolt-head flat orientation

steps.title: Remove the angle lever from the swingarm
steps.instruction: Remove the nut and bolt that hold the angle lever to the swingarm and lift the angle lever out. Keep the spacers and any thin washers on the lever and note which side they came from.
verification: Angle lever is off
Spacers and washers are with the lever and their sides are noted

steps.title: Remove the pull rod from the frame
steps.instruction: Remove the nut and bolt that hold the pull rod to the frame and take the pull rod off. Bag and label all three linkage bolts and nuts separately so each goes back in its own hole.
verification: Pull rod is off
Each linkage bolt is in its own labelled bag

steps.title: Pull the swingarm pivot shaft
steps.instruction: Hold the swingarm, remove the pivot nut, and push the pivot shaft out; tap it with a brass or plastic drift if it sticks rather than hammering on the threads. Note the flat on the shaft head and how it sits. Ease the swingarm rearward out of the frame, keeping the collar bushings from dropping on the floor.
verification: Swingarm is off the bike
Pivot shaft threads are undamaged
Collar bushings are recovered

steps.title: Strip and clean every part
steps.instruction: Pull the spacers and collar bushings out of the swingarm, angle lever and pull rod, wipe out the old grease, and wash everything in parts cleaner. Dry it with compressed air without spinning the bearings with the air jet. Lay the parts out by location.
verification: All parts are clean and dry
Parts are laid out by where they came from

steps.title: Check the swingarm for cracks and bends
steps.instruction: Look over the swingarm under good light, especially around the pivot, the linkage lugs, the axle slots and any welds. Any crack, bend or deformation means the swingarm must be replaced; it cannot be repaired.
verification: No cracks, bends or deformation found, or replacement ordered

steps.title: Inspect needle bearings, spacers and seals
steps.instruction: Roll each needle bearing in the angle lever and pull rod with your finger: it should feel smooth, with every needle present and no rust or flat spots. Check the spacers for a worn step, pitting or rust where the needles ride, and check the seals for tears or hardening. Mark every bearing, spacer or seal that is not perfect for replacement; on a race bike most people just replace all of them.
verification: Each bearing, spacer and seal has a keep or replace decision

steps.title: Measure and record the angle lever width
steps.instruction: Measure the overall width of the angle lever across the bosses where the thin spacing washers sit. It should be 54.91 to 55.00 mm (2.1618 to 2.1654 in). If it measures under that, add spacing washers to bring the stack back into range.
verification: Width recorded
Width is 54.91 to 55.00 mm, or spacing washers have been added to correct it

steps.title: Record how deep each needle bearing sits
steps.instruction: Before you press anything out, measure how far each linkage needle bearing sits below the face of its bore with a depth gauge or caliper, and write the number down for each position. These depths are not published, so the old bearings are your reference for fitting the new ones.
verification: Depth for every linkage bearing position is written down

steps.title: Remove linkage seals and old bearings
steps.instruction: Pry the seals out with a seal pick without scratching the bore. Press each old needle bearing out with a bearing tool or a socket just smaller than its outside diameter, supporting the part on the opposite face. Use a press or a drawbolt puller, not a hammer.
verification: Bores are empty, clean and free of score marks
Bearings came out without damaging the bore

steps.title: Press in new linkage needle bearings
steps.instruction: Press each new needle bearing in with the lettered end facing your tool, pushing only on the outer shell, until it reaches the depth you recorded for that bore. A stepped drift that locates in the bearing stops it from going in crooked. Spin each one with a finger afterwards to check that no needle was knocked out of place.
verification: Every new bearing sits at its recorded depth
All needles turn freely

steps.title: Grease the linkage and fit new seals
steps.instruction: Pack each needle bearing with long-life grease, press in new seals with grease on the lips, and slide the greased spacers back in. Refit any spacing washers on the angle lever on the sides you noted.
verification: Bearings packed with grease
New seals are flush and greased
Spacers and washers are in place

steps.title: Strip the left swingarm pivot bearing
steps.instruction: On the left pivot, pull the two collar bushings, slide out the inner bushing, lever out both radial shaft seals and remove the stop disks. Press the old bearing out with a suitable driver, supporting the swingarm so the pivot boss carries the load.
verification: Left bore is empty
Stop disks kept for reuse or replacement

steps.title: Build the left pivot bearing back up
steps.instruction: Press the new bearing squarely into the left bore with a driver on its outer edge. Fit the stop disks, then press in the new seals and slide the inner bushing back through.
verification: New bearing is square in the bore
Stop disks and new seals are fitted
Inner bushing slides through freely

steps.title: Strip the right swingarm pivot bearing
steps.instruction: On the right pivot, pull the collar bushings and the inner bushing, lever out the seals and press the old bearing out. The right side has no stop disks.
verification: Right bore is empty and undamaged

steps.title: Build the right pivot bearing back up
steps.instruction: Press the new bearing into the right bore, press in the new seals and refit the inner bushing.
verification: New bearing seated square
New seals fitted
Inner bushing in place

steps.title: Grease the pivot seals and fit the collars
steps.instruction: Coat the lips of all four pivot seals with long-life grease, then fit the collar bushings on both sides with their shoulders facing in toward the swingarm. Clean the pivot shaft and give it a light coat of grease.
verification: Seal lips greased
Collar shoulders face inward on both sides
Pivot shaft greased

steps.title: Fit the swingarm and torque the pivot
steps.instruction: Offer the swingarm up into the frame, keeping the collars in place, and slide the pivot shaft through with its head flat lined up as noted. Fit the nut and torque it to 100 Nm (73.8 lb-ft). Lift and drop the swingarm by hand: it should swing smoothly with no side play.
verification: Pivot nut torqued to 100 Nm (73.8 lb-ft)
Swingarm moves smoothly with no side play

steps.title: Bolt the pull rod to the frame
steps.instruction: Set the pull rod into its frame mount, slide its bolt through, and torque the nut to 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft).
verification: Frame-to-pull-rod nut torqued to 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft)

steps.title: Hang the angle lever on the swingarm, loose
steps.instruction: Fit the angle lever to the swingarm with its bolt and nut, but only run the nut on snug. It gets its final torque last, once everything is aligned.
verification: Angle lever is on with the nut snug but not torqued

steps.title: Fit the lower shock bolt, loose
steps.instruction: Clean the threads of the lower shock bolt, apply Loctite 2701, and pass it through the angle lever and shock eye. Run it in but do not torque it yet. Raising the swingarm slightly with the block helps line the holes up.
verification: Lower shock bolt is in with thread locker, not yet torqued

steps.title: Join the pull rod to the angle lever
steps.instruction: Line the pull rod up with the angle lever, slide the bolt through with its head flat seated the way you photographed it, and torque the nut to 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft).
verification: Bolt-head flat sits against its stop
Nut torqued to 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft)

steps.title: Final-torque the shock and angle lever bolts
steps.instruction: Torque the lower shock bolt to 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft), then torque the angle-lever-to-swingarm nut to 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft). Put a paint mark across each linkage nut and bolt so you can spot movement later.
verification: Lower shock bolt at 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft)
Angle lever nut at 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft)
All linkage fasteners paint-marked

steps.title: Work the rear suspension through its travel
steps.instruction: Remove the support block and lift the swingarm by hand through as much travel as you can. Movement should be smooth with no clicks, tight spots or side play. If anything binds, find out why now.
verification: Swingarm and linkage move smoothly
No binding or play

steps.title: Put the rear caliper back on its rail
steps.instruction: Slide the rear caliper back onto its rail on the swingarm and clip the brake hose back into its guide, following the original routing.
verification: Caliper is on its rail
Hose is in its guide and not twisted

steps.title: Route and join the chain
steps.instruction: Feed the chain around the swingarm, over the engine sprocket and back, then join it with the master link. Fit the clip so its closed end points the way the chain travels on the top run (toward the rear), and make sure it snaps fully into both pin grooves.
verification: Chain runs on the engine sprocket and is joined
Clip closed end faces the direction of chain travel and is seated

steps.title: Grease the rear seals and spacers
steps.instruction: Wipe the hub seals and the faces of both spacers clean, smear long-life grease on the seal lips and on the spacer faces, and push the spacers back into the seals. Clean the axle and give it a thin coat of the same grease.
verification: Seal lips and spacer faces are greased
Both spacers are seated in the hub
Axle is clean and lightly greased

steps.title: Set the wheel in and slide the axle through
steps.instruction: Lift the wheel into the swingarm, guiding the brake disc between the two pads in the caliper. Loop the chain onto the rear sprocket, then push the axle through from the side it came out of.
verification: Brake disc sits between the pads, not against the caliper body
Chain is on the rear sprocket
Axle passes through both adjusters and the hub

steps.title: Fit the adjuster and run the nut on loose
steps.instruction: Put the chain adjuster block back on the axle and spin the axle nut on by hand, leaving it loose. Check that both adjuster blocks are hooked correctly over the ends of their adjusting screws.
verification: Nut is on but not tight
Both adjusters sit properly on their adjusting screws

steps.title: Set and record chain tension
steps.instruction: With the bike on the stand, pull the chain upward at the rear end of the chain sliding piece on the swingarm while the bottom run stays tight, and measure the gap. The target is 58 to 61 mm (2.28 to 2.40 in). To change it, loosen the adjuster lock nuts and turn the adjusting screws on both sides by the same amount so the marks on the left and right adjusters line up with the same reference marks; that keeps the wheel straight. Check at two or three spots on the chain because chains wear unevenly, then tighten the lock nuts.
verification: Measured tension is within 58 to 61 mm at the tightest spot
Left and right adjuster marks line up with the same reference
Adjuster lock nuts are tight

steps.title: Torque the rear axle nut
steps.instruction: Confirm both adjusters are still seated on their screws, then torque the rear axle nut to 80 Nm (59 lb-ft). Recheck the chain gap once more after torquing.
verification: Axle nut torqued to 80 Nm (59 lb-ft)
Chain tension still within 58 to 61 mm

steps.title: Pump the rear brake up
steps.instruction: Press the rear brake pedal several times until the pads meet the disc and the pedal firms up. Spin the wheel to make sure the brake releases and only drags lightly.
verification: Pedal is firm
Wheel spins freely after the pedal is released

steps.title: Check rear brake pedal free play
steps.instruction: Unhook the pedal return spring, move the pedal between its stop and the point where it touches the master cylinder piston, and measure the free play at the pedal tip. It should be 3 to 5 mm (0.12 to 0.20 in). Reconnect the spring.
verification: Pedal free play is 3 to 5 mm
Return spring reconnected

steps.title: Refit the frame protectors
steps.instruction: Set the left protector in place, slide the right one in from underneath and push it back, then fit the screws with their bushings and tighten them to 3 Nm (2.2 lb-ft). Replace the cable ties you cut.
verification: Protector screws at 3 Nm (2.2 lb-ft)
Cable ties replaced

steps.title: Final check and test ride
steps.instruction: Take the bike off the stand, push down on the seat a few times to check the rear moves freely, and go over every fastener you touched. Ride a few easy laps, then recheck chain tension and swingarm play once it cools.
verification: Rear suspension moves freely
All touched fasteners checked
Chain tension and play rechecked after the first ride

verification: Every new bearing sits at its recorded depth
All needles turn freely

steps.title: Grease the linkage and fit new seals
steps.instruction: Pack each needle bearing with long-life grease, press in new seals with grease on the lips, and slide the greased spacers back in. Refit any spacing washers on the angle lever on the sides you noted.
verification: Bearings packed with grease
New seals are flush and greased
Spacers and washers are in place

steps.title: Strip the left swingarm pivot bearing
steps.instruction: On the left pivot, pull the two collar bushings, slide out the inner bushing, lever out both radial shaft seals and remove the stop disks. Press the old bearing out with a suitable driver, supporting the swingarm so the pivot boss carries the load.
verification: Left bore is empty
Stop disks kept for reuse or replacement

steps.title: Build the left pivot bearing back up
steps.instruction: Press the new bearing squarely into the left bore with a driver on its outer edge. Fit the stop disks, then press in the new seals and slide the inner bushing back through.
verification: New bearing is square in the bore
Stop disks and new seals are fitted
Inner bushing slides through freely

steps.title: Strip the right swingarm pivot bearing
steps.instruction: On the right pivot, pull the collar bushings and the inner bushing, lever out the seals and press the old bearing out. The right side has no stop disks.
verification: Right bore is empty and undamaged

steps.title: Build the right pivot bearing back up
steps.instruction: Press the new bearing into the right bore, press in the new seals and refit the inner bushing.
verification: New bearing seated square
New seals fitted
Inner bushing in place

steps.title: Grease the pivot seals and fit the collars
steps.instruction: Coat the lips of all four pivot seals with long-life grease, then fit the collar bushings on both sides with their shoulders facing in toward the swingarm. Clean the pivot shaft and give it a light coat of grease.
verification: Seal lips greased
Collar shoulders face inward on both sides
Pivot shaft greased

steps.title: Fit the swingarm and torque the pivot
steps.instruction: Offer the swingarm up into the frame, keeping the collars in place, and slide the pivot shaft through with its head flat lined up as noted. Fit the nut and torque it to 100 Nm (73.8 lb-ft). Lift and drop the swingarm by hand: it should swing smoothly with no side play.
verification: Pivot nut torqued to 100 Nm (73.8 lb-ft)
Swingarm moves smoothly with no side play

steps.title: Bolt the pull rod to the frame
steps.instruction: Set the pull rod into its frame mount, slide its bolt through, and torque the nut to 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft).
verification: Frame-to-pull-rod nut torqued to 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft)

steps.title: Hang the angle lever on the swingarm, loose
steps.instruction: Fit the angle lever to the swingarm with its bolt and nut, but only run the nut on snug. It gets its final torque last, once everything is aligned.
verification: Angle lever is on with the nut snug but not torqued

steps.title: Fit the lower shock bolt, loose
steps.instruction: Clean the threads of the lower shock bolt, apply Loctite 2701, and pass it through the angle lever and shock eye. Run it in but do not torque it yet. Raising the swingarm slightly with the block helps line the holes up.
verification: Lower shock bolt is in with thread locker, not yet torqued

steps.title: Join the pull rod to the angle lever
steps.instruction: Line the pull rod up with the angle lever, slide the bolt through with its head flat seated the way you photographed it, and torque the nut to 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft).
verification: Bolt-head flat sits against its stop
Nut torqued to 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft)

steps.title: Final-torque the shock and angle lever bolts
steps.instruction: Torque the lower shock bolt to 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft), then torque the angle-lever-to-swingarm nut to 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft). Put a paint mark across each linkage nut and bolt so you can spot movement later.
verification: Lower shock bolt at 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft)
Angle lever nut at 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft)
All linkage fasteners paint-marked

steps.title: Work the rear suspension through its travel
steps.instruction: Remove the support block and lift the swingarm by hand through as much travel as you can. Movement should be smooth with no clicks, tight spots or side play. If anything binds, find out why now.
verification: Swingarm and linkage move smoothly
No binding or play

steps.title: Put the rear caliper back on its rail
steps.instruction: Slide the rear caliper back onto its rail on the swingarm and clip the brake hose back into its guide, following the original routing.
verification: Caliper is on its rail
Hose is in its guide and not twisted

steps.title: Route and join the chain
steps.instruction: Feed the chain around the swingarm, over the engine sprocket and back, then join it with the master link. Fit the clip so its closed end points the way the chain travels on the top run (toward the rear), and make sure it snaps fully into both pin grooves.
verification: Chain runs on the engine sprocket and is joined
Clip closed end faces the direction of chain travel and is seated

steps.title: Grease the rear seals and spacers
steps.instruction: Wipe the hub seals and the faces of both spacers clean, smear long-life grease on the seal lips and on the spacer faces, and push the spacers back into the seals. Clean the axle and give it a thin coat of the same grease.
verification: Seal lips and spacer faces are greased
Both spacers are seated in the hub
Axle is clean and lightly greased

steps.title: Set the wheel in and slide the axle through
steps.instruction: Lift the wheel into the swingarm, guiding the brake disc between the two pads in the caliper. Loop the chain onto the rear sprocket, then push the axle through from the side it came out of.
verification: Brake disc sits between the pads, not against the caliper body
Chain is on the rear sprocket
Axle passes through both adjusters and the hub

steps.title: Fit the adjuster and run the nut on loose
steps.instruction: Put the chain adjuster block back on the axle and spin the axle nut on by hand, leaving it loose. Check that both adjuster blocks are hooked correctly over the ends of their adjusting screws.
verification: Nut is on but not tight
Both adjusters sit properly on their adjusting screws

steps.title: Set and record chain tension
steps.instruction: With the bike on the stand, pull the chain upward at the rear end of the chain sliding piece on the swingarm while the bottom run stays tight, and measure the gap. The target is 58 to 61 mm (2.28 to 2.40 in). To change it, loosen the adjuster lock nuts and turn the adjusting screws on both sides by the same amount so the marks on the left and right adjusters line up with the same reference marks; that keeps the wheel straight. Check at two or three spots on the chain because chains wear unevenly, then tighten the lock nuts.
verification: Measured tension is within 58 to 61 mm at the tightest spot
Left and right adjuster marks line up with the same reference
Adjuster lock nuts are tight

steps.title: Torque the rear axle nut
steps.instruction: Confirm both adjusters are still seated on their screws, then torque the rear axle nut to 80 Nm (59 lb-ft). Recheck the chain gap once more after torquing.
verification: Axle nut torqued to 80 Nm (59 lb-ft)
Chain tension still within 58 to 61 mm

steps.title: Pump the rear brake up
steps.instruction: Press the rear brake pedal several times until the pads meet the disc and the pedal firms up. Spin the wheel to make sure the brake releases and only drags lightly.
verification: Pedal is firm
Wheel spins freely after the pedal is released

steps.title: Check rear brake pedal free play
steps.instruction: Unhook the pedal return spring, move the pedal between its stop and the point where it touches the master cylinder piston, and measure the free play at the pedal tip. It should be 3 to 5 mm (0.12 to 0.20 in). Reconnect the spring.
verification: Pedal free play is 3 to 5 mm
Return spring reconnected

steps.title: Refit the frame protectors
steps.instruction: Set the left protector in place, slide the right one in from underneath and push it back, then fit the screws with their bushings and tighten them to 3 Nm (2.2 lb-ft). Replace the cable ties you cut.
verification: Protector screws at 3 Nm (2.2 lb-ft)
Cable ties replaced

steps.title: Final check and test ride
steps.instruction: Take the bike off the stand, push down on the seat a few times to check the rear moves freely, and go over every fastener you touched. Ride a few easy laps, then recheck chain tension and swingarm play once it cools.
verification: Rear suspension moves freely
All touched fasteners checked
Chain tension and play rechecked after the first ride

verification: Work area is free of mud and grit
Parts tray and labelled bags are ready

steps.title: Put the bike on the lift stand
steps.instruction: Pull the plug-in stand out of the rear axle and lift the bike onto a lift stand, placing it under the frame below the engine. Both wheels should hang free. Rock the bike gently to make sure it sits square and cannot tip, and keep anyone off it while it is up.
verification: Both wheels are off the ground
Bike is stable when pushed lightly from each side

steps.title: Check the steering before you start
steps.instruction: With the bars straight, push the fork legs forward and back and feel for a clunk at the steering head. Then turn the bars slowly lock to lock and feel for notches or a spot where the steering wants to stop in the center. Note what you find.
verification: Play and notchiness noted

steps.title: Push the front caliper pistons back
steps.instruction: Press the front caliper toward the disc by hand to nudge the pistons back slightly. Do not lever against the spokes while you do it.
verification: Pads have a little clearance from the disc

steps.title: Loosen the front axle screw and clamps
steps.instruction: Back the front axle screw out several turns but leave it engaged, then loosen the fork-foot pinch screws. Push on the head of the axle screw to drive the axle out of the clamp on the far side, then unscrew and remove the axle screw.
verification: Pinch screws are loose
Axle has moved free of the clamp
Axle screw is out and bagged

steps.title: Pull the axle and drop the wheel out
steps.instruction: Support the wheel, slide the axle out, and roll the wheel forward out of the fork. Lay it down so the disc is protected and pull the two spacers out of the hub seals. Do not squeeze the front brake lever while the wheel is out; slip a spacer or a folded piece of cardboard between the pads if you have one.
verification: Wheel is out and the disc is protected
Both front spacers are accounted for
Front brake lever has not been squeezed

steps.title: Unbolt the front caliper and hang it
steps.instruction: Remove the screws on the brake hose clamp at the fork guard, then remove the two caliper screws and lift the caliper off. Hang it from the frame with a tie so the hose has no tension or kinks.
verification: Caliper hangs on a tie
Brake hose is not kinked

steps.title: Remove the front number plate
steps.instruction: Remove the number plate screw, unhook the plate from the brake hose and lift it off.
verification: Number plate is off

steps.title: Remove the front fender
steps.instruction: Remove the fender screws and lift the fender off the bottom clamp.
verification: Fender is off
Screws are bagged

steps.title: Photograph fork height and orientation
steps.instruction: Take a photo of each fork tube where it exits the top clamp. At stock height, count down from the top of the tube: groove number two lines up level with the top face of the upper clamp. The right leg is the damping leg with its bleeder screw facing forward; the left leg is the air leg with its air valve facing forward.
verification: Photos show groove position and which leg is which

steps.title: Pull the left fork leg
steps.instruction: Loosen the top and bottom clamp pinch screws on the left leg and slide the leg down and out with a slight twist. Lay it somewhere it cannot roll off the bench.
verification: Left leg is out and safe

steps.title: Pull the right fork leg
steps.instruction: Do the same on the right: loosen both pinch screws and slide the leg out.
verification: Right leg is out and safe

steps.title: Take off the handlebar pad
steps.instruction: Pull the handlebar pad off the bar so you can get to the top clamp fasteners.
verification: Top clamp fasteners are accessible

steps.title: Undo the top clamp fasteners
steps.instruction: Remove the screw holding the wiring harness holder and move the harness out of the way. Remove the M8 steering stem screw in the top clamp, then remove the large M20 steering head screw in the center of the top clamp.
verification: Harness is detached from the clamp
M8 stem screw and M20 head screw are out and bagged

steps.title: Lift off the top clamp with the bars
steps.instruction: Lift the top clamp off the stem with the handlebar still attached and rest it on a towel over the tank or a box beside the bike. Keep the clutch line, brake hose, throttle cables and wiring free of sharp bends.
verification: Top clamp is off and supported
No line or cable is kinked or stretched

steps.title: Remove the seal and drop the bottom clamp
steps.instruction: Pull the steering head seal off the top of the stem. Hold the bottom clamp, slide it down and out of the frame, and catch the upper bearing as it comes free.
verification: Bottom clamp with stem is out
Upper bearing and seal recovered

steps.title: Clean bearings, races and seals
steps.instruction: Wash the old grease off both bearings, the races in the frame, the stem and the seals with parts cleaner, and dry everything. You cannot judge a bearing that is still covered in grease.
verification: All bearing surfaces are clean and dry

steps.title: Inspect and decide: regrease or replace
steps.instruction: Look at the races in the frame and the rollers on both bearings for dents, pitting, rust or dull bands. Small dents in the races at the straight-ahead position are what causes notchy steering. If the bearings and races are perfect, skip to greasing. If any part is marked, replace both bearings, both races and the seals as a set.
verification: Decision made: regrease only, or full bearing and race replacement

steps.title: Remove the lower race from the frame
steps.instruction: Use the KTM tool bracket 58429089000 with pressing tool A46029092000 to pull the lower race out of the steering head. Keep the tool square so it does not chew the bore.
verification: Lower race is out
Frame bore is undamaged

steps.title: Press in the new lower race
steps.instruction: Press the new lower race into the frame until it bottoms out, using tool bracket 58429089000 with pressing tool 58429091000.
verification: New lower race is fully bottomed with no gap

steps.title: Remove the upper race and seal
steps.instruction: Pull the upper race out with tool bracket 58429089000 and pressing tool A46029092000, then remove the seal ring from the top of the head tube.
verification: Upper race and seal are out
Bore is clean

steps.title: Press in the new upper race and seal
steps.instruction: Press the new upper race in until it bottoms, using tool bracket 58429089000 with pressing tool 58429091000. Grease a new seal ring and fit it.
verification: Upper race fully bottomed
New greased seal fitted

steps.title: Replace the lower bearing on the stem
steps.instruction: Pull the old lower bearing off the stem with a bearing separator, then remove the seal ring under it. Grease and fit a new seal, then press the new bearing onto the stem with a tube that bears only on the inner race, until it stops.
verification: New seal under the bearing
New bearing pressed fully down on the inner race only

steps.title: Pack the bearings with grease
steps.instruction: Work high-viscosity grease (SKF LGHB 2 or equivalent) fully into both bearings and put a coat on both races and the seal lips.
verification: Both bearings packed
Races and seal lips greased

steps.title: Install the bottom clamp and upper bearing
steps.instruction: Slide the stem up through the head tube, drop the greased upper bearing over the stem into its race, and push the steering head seal down over it.
verification: Stem is fully home
Upper bearing and seal seated

steps.title: Fit the top clamp with the M20 screw loose
steps.instruction: Set the top clamp with the bars onto the stem and thread in the M20 steering head screw, but do not tighten it yet.
verification: Top clamp on and M20 screw started by hand

steps.title: Slide both fork legs back in
steps.instruction: Push both legs up through the clamps: damping leg on the right with its bleeder screw forward, air leg on the left with its valve forward. Line groove number two (counting down from the top) up level with the top face of the upper clamp, matching your photos.
verification: Legs on the correct sides and facing correctly
Fork height matches the photos on both sides

steps.title: Torque the bottom clamp pinch screws
steps.instruction: Torque the bottom clamp pinch screws on both legs to 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft).
verification: Bottom clamp screws at 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft)

steps.title: Torque the M20 steering head screw
steps.instruction: Torque the M20 steering head screw to 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft). This sets the bearing preload.
verification: M20 head screw at 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft)

steps.title: Fit the M8 stem screw with thread locker
steps.instruction: Put Loctite 243 on the M8 steering stem screw, fit it, and torque to 20 Nm (14.8 lb-ft).
verification: M8 stem screw at 20 Nm (14.8 lb-ft) with thread locker

steps.title: Settle the clamp and torque the top pinch screws
steps.instruction: Give the top clamp a few light taps with a plastic mallet to relieve any stress, then torque the top clamp pinch screws on both legs to 17 Nm (12.5 lb-ft).
verification: Top clamp screws at 17 Nm (12.5 lb-ft)

steps.title: Reattach the wiring harness holder
steps.instruction: Clip the wiring harness back into its holder on the left and fit its screw.
verification: Harness is secured to the clamp

steps.title: Bolt the front caliper back on
steps.instruction: Put Loctite 243 on the caliper screws, fit the caliper, and torque to 25 Nm (18.4 lb-ft). Refit the brake hose clamp on the fork guard.
verification: Caliper screws at 25 Nm (18.4 lb-ft) with thread locker
Hose clamp refitted

steps.title: Refit the fender, bar pad and number plate
steps.instruction: Fit the front fender and torque its screws to 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft). Push the bar pad back on. Clip the brake hose into the holders on the number plate, set the plate so its lugs engage the fender, and fit its screw.
verification: Fender screws at 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft)
Number plate lugs engaged and hose in its holders

steps.title: Grease the front seals and spacers
steps.instruction: Clean the hub seal lips and both spacer faces, coat them with long-life grease, and press the spacers back into the seals. Clean the axle and give it a light film of grease.
verification: Seals and spacer faces greased
Spacers seated
Axle lightly greased

steps.title: Set the front wheel in the fork
steps.instruction: Remove anything you wedged between the pads, lift the wheel into the fork guiding the disc between the pads, and slide the axle through both fork feet.
verification: Disc is between the pads
Axle passes through both fork feet

steps.title: Torque the front axle screw
steps.instruction: Fit the axle screw and torque it to 35 Nm (25.8 lb-ft), leaving the fork-foot pinch screws loose for now. Pump the front brake lever until it is firm and the pads are seated.
verification: Axle screw torqued to 35 Nm (25.8 lb-ft)
Brake lever is firm

steps.title: Let the fork settle, then tighten the pinch screws
steps.instruction: Take the bike off the stand, hold the front brake on and push the fork down hard a few times so the legs line up naturally on the axle. Then tighten the fork-foot pinch screws to 15 Nm (11.1 lb-ft).
verification: Fork compresses smoothly without binding
Fork-foot pinch screws torqued to 15 Nm (11.1 lb-ft)

steps.title: Check cables and lines lock to lock
steps.instruction: Turn the bars fully left and right and watch the brake hose, clutch line, throttle cables and wiring. Nothing should stretch, pinch or snag.
verification: All lines move freely through full lock

steps.title: Check and, if needed, adjust steering play
steps.instruction: Lift the front off the ground again, rock the fork forward and back and feel for play, then swing the bars lock to lock. You want zero play and smooth movement with no notches. verification: No play at the steering head
Steering is smooth with no notches

steps.title: Final check and test ride
steps.instruction: Off the stand, squeeze the front brake and pump the fork. Check the fork air pressure since the legs were handled. Ride gently first, then recheck steering play after the first ride.
verification: Brake is firm
Steering checked again after the first ride

critical_stop_conditions: Hub bore scored or a new bearing pushes in by hand: stop, the hub needs replacing
Lock ring will not click fully into its groove: stop, the bearing is not fully seated
Rear disc under 3.5 mm, cracked or warped: replace the disc and fit new pads with it
Chain tension cannot be brought into 58 to 61 mm with the wheel straight: the chain is worn or the wrong length, stop and check the drivetrain

steps.title: Wash the work area first
steps.instruction: Wash and dry the bike before you open anything, paying extra attention to the area you are about to work on. Grit that falls into an open bearing bore or brake system is how good parts fail early. Have a clean tray and zip bags with a marker ready for fasteners.
verification: Work area is free of mud and grit
Parts tray and labelled bags are ready

steps.title: Put the bike on the lift stand
steps.instruction: Pull the plug-in stand out of the rear axle and lift the bike onto a lift stand, placing it under the frame below the engine. Both wheels should hang free. Rock the bike gently to make sure it sits square and cannot tip, and keep anyone off it while it is up.
verification: Both wheels are off the ground
Bike is stable when pushed lightly from each side

steps.title: Check rear wheel bearing play
steps.instruction: Hold the swingarm and rock the top of the rear wheel side to side. A knock means the hub bearings need replacing. Spin it and listen for grinding too.
verification: Play or roughness noted

steps.title: Push the rear caliper piston back
steps.instruction: Squeeze the rear caliper toward the disc by hand to push the piston back a little; this gives the pads clearance so the wheel comes out and goes back in easily. Keep the caliper away from the spokes while you push.
verification: Pads are no longer dragging hard on the disc

steps.title: Remove the rear axle nut and adjuster
steps.instruction: Spin off the rear axle nut and lift off that side's chain adjuster block. Slide the axle out only part of the way, just enough that the wheel can roll forward in the swingarm.
verification: Nut and adjuster are bagged together
Axle is still holding the wheel

steps.title: Roll the wheel forward and lift the chain off
steps.instruction: Push the wheel as far forward as it will go to create slack, then lift the chain off the rear sprocket and lay it over a rag on the swingarm so it does not scratch anything.
verification: Chain is off the rear sprocket

steps.title: Pull the axle and lift the wheel out
steps.instruction: Hold the wheel up with one hand, pull the axle out, and lower the wheel out of the swingarm. Set it down on blocks or on its side with the brake disc facing up so the disc cannot be bent or contaminated. Take the two spacers out of the hub seals and keep them with the axle. From here on, do not touch the rear brake pedal.
verification: Wheel is out and resting so the disc carries no load
Both hub spacers are accounted for
Rear brake pedal has not been pressed

steps.title: Lever out the rear hub seals
steps.instruction: Support the wheel on blocks with the hub clear of the bench and lever the seals out of both sides of the hub without gouging the bore.
verification: Seals are out
Bores undamaged

steps.title: Drive out the sprocket-side bearing
steps.instruction: Working from the brake-disc side through the hub, drive the sprocket-side bearing out from the inside toward the outside, moving the drift around its inner edge in small steps.
verification: Sprocket-side bearing is out

steps.title: Remove and check the spacer washer and tube
steps.instruction: Take out the spacer washer behind that bearing and check it for wear or damage; replace it if it is marked. Then lift out the center spacer tube.
verification: Spacer washer judged good or replaced
Spacer tube is out

steps.title: Remove the lock ring and brake-side bearing
steps.instruction: On the brake-disc side, remove the lock ring with circlip pliers, then drive that bearing out from the inside toward the outside.
verification: Lock ring and brake-side bearing are out

steps.title: Clean and inspect the rear hub
steps.instruction: Clean both bores, the lock ring groove and the spacer tube, and check the bores for scoring or spun-bearing marks.
verification: Bores clean and undamaged
Lock ring groove clean

steps.title: Press in the new brake-side bearing
steps.instruction: From the outside, press the new brake-side bearing in until it bottoms, pushing only on the outer race. Then fit the lock ring and listen for the click as it snaps into its groove.
verification: Bearing bottomed
Lock ring clicked into its groove

steps.title: Grease and fit the spacer tube and washer
steps.instruction: Clean and grease the spacer tube and drop it into the hub from the sprocket side, then put the spacer washer in place.
verification: Spacer tube and washer in place

steps.title: Press in the new sprocket-side bearing
steps.instruction: Press the new sprocket-side bearing in from the outside on its outer race until it stops. Check that both bearings spin smoothly.
verification: Bearing bottomed
Both bearings turn smoothly

steps.title: Fit new rear hub seals
steps.instruction: Grease two new radial shaft seals and press them in on each side until they sit flush with the hub.
verification: Seals flush and greased

steps.title: Check the rear disc and sprocket while you are here
steps.instruction: Measure the rear disc thickness where the pads run; the minimum is 3.5 mm (0.138 in). Look for cracks or warping, and look over the sprocket for hooked or thin teeth.
verification: Disc thickness recorded and at least 3.5 mm
Sprocket condition noted

steps.title: Grease the rear seals and spacers
steps.instruction: Wipe the hub seals and the faces of both spacers clean, smear long-life grease on the seal lips and on the spacer faces, and push the spacers back into the seals. Clean the axle and give it a thin coat of the same grease.
verification: Seal lips and spacer faces are greased
Both spacers are seated in the hub
Axle is clean and lightly greased

steps.title: Set the wheel in and slide the axle through
steps.instruction: Lift the wheel into the swingarm, guiding the brake disc between the two pads in the caliper. Loop the chain onto the rear sprocket, then push the axle through from the side it came out of.
verification: Brake disc sits between the pads, not against the caliper body
Chain is on the rear sprocket
Axle passes through both adjusters and the hub

steps.title: Fit the adjuster and run the nut on loose
steps.instruction: Put the chain adjuster block back on the axle and spin the axle nut on by hand, leaving it loose. Check that both adjuster blocks are hooked correctly over the ends of their adjusting screws.
verification: Nut is on but not tight
Both adjusters sit properly on their adjusting screws

steps.title: Set and record chain tension
steps.instruction: With the bike on the stand, pull the chain upward at the rear end of the chain sliding piece on the swingarm while the bottom run stays tight, and measure the gap. The target is 58 to 61 mm (2.28 to 2.40 in). To change it, loosen the adjuster lock nuts and turn the adjusting screws on both sides by the same amount so the marks on the left and right adjusters line up with the same reference marks; that keeps the wheel straight. Check at two or three spots on the chain because chains wear unevenly, then tighten the lock nuts.
verification: Measured tension is within 58 to 61 mm at the tightest spot
Left and right adjuster marks line up with the same reference
Adjuster lock nuts are tight

steps.title: Torque the rear axle nut
steps.instruction: Confirm both adjusters are still seated on their screws, then torque the rear axle nut to 80 Nm (59 lb-ft). Recheck the chain gap once more after torquing.
verification: Axle nut torqued to 80 Nm (59 lb-ft)
Chain tension still within 58 to 61 mm

steps.title: Pump the rear brake up
steps.instruction: Press the rear brake pedal several times until the pads meet the disc and the pedal firms up. Spin the wheel to make sure the brake releases and only drags lightly.
verification: Pedal is firm
Wheel spins freely after the pedal is released

steps.title: Spin, brake and ride
steps.instruction: Off the stand, spin the wheel, press the brake, and push the bike to feel for drag. Ride gently first and recheck chain tension and wheel play once it cools.
verification: Wheel spins freely
Brake firm
Chain tension and play rechecked after the first ride

exit_state: New chain, engine sprocket and rear sprocket fitted; chain tension set, all covers back on; ready to ride.

completeness: Checks chain, guide and slider wear, then replaces the chain, engine sprocket and rear sprocket together with tension and alignment set; chain guide, slider and sliding piece replacement are flagged but not walked through.
excluded: Chain guide, chain sliding guard and sliding piece replacement

Master link clip not fully seated or facing the wrong way: stop and refit it
Chain tension cannot reach 58 to 61 mm with the wheel straight: wrong chain length, stop

steps.instruction: Wash and dry the bike before you open anything, paying extra attention to the area you are about to work on. Grit that falls into an open bearing bore or brake system is how good parts fail early. Have a clean tray and zip bags with a marker ready for fasteners.
verification: Work area is free of mud and grit
Parts tray and labelled bags are ready

steps.title: Put the bike on the lift stand
steps.instruction: Pull the plug-in stand out of the rear axle and lift the bike onto a lift stand, placing it under the frame below the engine. Both wheels should hang free. Rock the bike gently to make sure it sits square and cannot tip, and keep anyone off it while it is up.
verification: Both wheels are off the ground
Bike is stable when pushed lightly from each side

steps.title: Measure chain wear
steps.instruction: Shift to neutral. Pull up on the top run with about 10 to 15 kg (22 to 33 lb) of force and measure across 18 rollers on the bottom run. The maximum is 272 mm (10.71 in); check a few spots and record the longest. Even if you are replacing everything anyway, the number tells you how fast your chain wears.
verification: Longest 18-roller measurement recorded

steps.title: Check the chain guide, slider and sliding piece
steps.instruction: Measure the chain guide thickness with a caliper; the minimum is 6 mm (0.24 in). Look at the chain sliding guard on the swingarm and the chain sliding piece: once they are worn so thin that the chain pins sit level with or below their wearing surface, replace them. Make sure each one is tight.
verification: Chain guide at least 6 mm, or replacement planned
Slider and sliding piece judged good or replaced

steps.title: Remove the air filter box cover
steps.instruction: Remove the screw securing the air filter box cover if it has one, then pull the cover out at its rear corner, push it sideways and forward, and lift it off.
verification: Air filter box cover is off and the filter is not disturbed

steps.title: Remove the left frame protector
steps.instruction: Cut the cable ties and remove the left frame protector screws and bushings, then lift the protector off.
verification: Left frame protector is off

steps.title: Remove the engine sprocket cover
steps.instruction: Remove the M6 screw with its washer and the M8 screw from the engine sprocket cover and slide the cover forward off its holder. Clean out the packed dirt behind it.
verification: Sprocket cover is off
Area behind it is clean

steps.title: Break loose the engine sprocket screw
steps.instruction: Have a helper stand on the rear brake to lock the wheel, then remove the engine sprocket screw and its washer. The chain must still be fitted for this.
verification: Engine sprocket screw and washer are out

steps.title: Split and remove the old chain
steps.instruction: Bring the master link round to the rear sprocket, pop off the clip, take off the side plate, push the link out and pull the chain off.
verification: Old chain is off

steps.title: Push the rear caliper piston back
steps.instruction: Squeeze the rear caliper toward the disc by hand to push the piston back a little; this gives the pads clearance so the wheel comes out and goes back in easily. Keep the caliper away from the spokes while you push.
verification: Pads are no longer dragging hard on the disc

steps.title: Take the rear wheel out
steps.instruction: Remove the axle nut and adjuster, support the wheel and pull the axle, then lift the wheel out and set it down with the disc protected. Keep the spacers with the axle and do not press the brake pedal.
verification: Wheel is out
Spacers are accounted for

steps.title: Slide off the engine sprocket
steps.instruction: Slide the engine sprocket off the countershaft splines. Wipe the splines and the shaft seal area clean and look for oil weeping at the seal.
verification: Sprocket off
Countershaft splines clean

steps.title: Remove the rear sprocket
steps.instruction: Remove the rear sprocket nuts and screws and lift the sprocket off. Clean the hub face so the new sprocket sits flat.
verification: Old sprocket off
Hub face clean

steps.title: Fit the new rear sprocket
steps.instruction: Set the new sprocket on the hub, fit the screws with Loctite 2701, and torque the nuts to 35 Nm (25.8 lb-ft) in a crisscross pattern. Stock gearing is 13:51.
verification: Sprocket nuts at 35 Nm (25.8 lb-ft) with thread locker
Sprocket sits flat on the hub

steps.title: Slide on the new engine sprocket
steps.instruction: Slide the new engine sprocket onto the countershaft splines with the same face outward as the old one. Leave the screw out for now.
verification: Sprocket is on the splines facing the right way

steps.title: Check the wheel bearings and refit the wheel
steps.instruction: Turn the hub bearings with a finger; if they are rough or loose, replace them before going further. Grease the seals and spacer faces, fit the spacers, and set the wheel into the swingarm with the disc between the pads. Slide the greased axle through.
verification: Wheel bearings smooth
Wheel and axle fitted

steps.title: Check the new chain length
steps.instruction: Lay the new chain beside the old one and match the link count. If it needs shortening, cut it with a chain breaker so the joint ends up as a master link, not a riveted pin you have broken.
verification: New chain has the same link count as the old one

steps.title: Fit and join the new chain
steps.instruction: Route the chain over the engine sprocket, through the guides and onto the rear sprocket, then join it with the master link. Point the closed end of the clip in the direction the chain moves, and check it snaps into both pin grooves.
verification: Chain joined
Clip closed end faces the direction of travel and is fully seated

steps.title: Fit the adjuster and run the nut on loose
steps.instruction: Put the chain adjuster back on the axle and spin the axle nut on loosely. Both adjusters must sit properly on their adjusting screws.
verification: Nut loose
Both adjusters seated on their screws

steps.title: Set and record chain tension
steps.instruction: With the bike on the stand, pull the chain upward at the rear end of the chain sliding piece on the swingarm while the bottom run stays tight, and measure the gap. The target is 58 to 61 mm (2.28 to 2.40 in). To change it, loosen the adjuster lock nuts and turn the adjusting screws on both sides by the same amount so the marks on the left and right adjusters line up with the same reference marks; that keeps the wheel straight. Check at two or three spots on the chain because chains wear unevenly, then tighten the lock nuts.
verification: Measured tension is within 58 to 61 mm at the tightest spot
Left and right adjuster marks line up with the same reference
Adjuster lock nuts are tight

steps.title: Torque the rear axle nut
steps.instruction: Confirm both adjusters are still seated on their screws, then torque the rear axle nut to 80 Nm (59 lb-ft). Recheck the chain gap once more after torquing.
verification: Axle nut torqued to 80 Nm (59 lb-ft)
Chain tension still within 58 to 61 mm

steps.title: Pump the rear brake up
steps.instruction: Press the rear brake pedal several times until the pads meet the disc and the pedal firms up. Spin the wheel to make sure the brake releases and only drags lightly.
verification: Pedal is firm
Wheel spins freely after the pedal is released

steps.title: Torque the engine sprocket screw
steps.instruction: Put Loctite 2701 on the engine sprocket screw, fit it with its washer, and with a helper holding the rear brake, torque it to 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft).
verification: Engine sprocket screw at 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft) with thread locker

steps.title: Refit the engine sprocket cover
steps.instruction: Slide the cover into its holder, fit the M6 screw with its washer at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft) and the M8 screw at 15 Nm (11.1 lb-ft).
verification: M6 at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft)
M8 at 15 Nm (11.1 lb-ft)

steps.title: Refit the frame protector and airbox cover
steps.instruction: Fit the left frame protector screws with their bushings at 3 Nm (2.2 lb-ft) and replace the cable ties. Hook the air filter box cover in at the front and clip it in at the back, then fit its screw if your bike uses one.
verification: Protector at 3 Nm (2.2 lb-ft)
Airbox cover fully clipped in

steps.title: Lube the new chain
steps.instruction: Spin the wheel and spray an off-road chain lube along the inside of the bottom run. Wipe off any that lands on the tire or disc with brake cleaner.
verification: Chain lubed
No lube on tire or disc

steps.title: Final check, ride, recheck tension
steps.instruction: Spin the wheel to check the chain runs straight onto both sprockets. Ride a few easy laps, then recheck chain tension once it cools; new chains stretch most at the start.
verification: Chain tracks straight
Tension rechecked after the first ride

exit_state: New chain, engine sprocket and rear sprocket fitted; chain tension set, all covers back on; ready to ride.

prerequisites: Brake discs checked: if a disc must be replaced, fit new pads at the same time
critical_stop_conditions: Disc below 2.5 mm front or 3.5 mm rear, cracked or warped: replace the disc and pads together

Parts tray and labelled bags are ready

steps.title: Measure pads and discs
steps.instruction: Look at the pads from the open side of each caliper and measure the friction material that is left. Below 1 mm (0.04 in), or any crack or contamination, means new pads. Measure each disc where the pads run: front minimum 2.5 mm (0.098 in), rear minimum 3.5 mm (0.138 in).
verification: Front and rear pad thickness recorded
Front and rear disc thickness recorded

steps.title: Level and open the clutch reservoir
steps.instruction: Turn the bars so the clutch reservoir on the left of the handlebar is level, wrap rags around it and over the tank and plastics, then remove the cover screws and lift off the cover and membrane.
verification: Reservoir level and open
Paint covered

steps.title: Pull out the old fluid in the reservoir
steps.instruction: Suck the old fluid out of the reservoir with a syringe; leave the bottom of the reservoir just wet so no air enters the master cylinder.
verification: Old fluid removed from the reservoir

steps.title: Fill the syringe with fresh fluid
steps.instruction: Fill a clean bleeding syringe (KTM 50329050000 or similar) with fresh DOT 4 or DOT 5.1 brake fluid and fit a short length of clear hose that fits snugly on a bleeder nipple. Push out any air bubbles from the syringe.
verification: Syringe full with no air in it

steps.title: Connect the syringe to the slave cylinder
steps.instruction: Follow the clutch line down to the slave cylinder on the engine, pull the dust cap off its bleeder screw and push the syringe hose on.
verification: Syringe hose is tight on the slave cylinder bleeder

steps.title: Crack the slave bleeder
steps.instruction: Open the slave bleeder just enough that fluid can be pushed in with the syringe, no more.
verification: Bleeder open a small amount

steps.title: Push fluid up through the system
steps.instruction: Press the syringe steadily so fresh fluid flows up from the slave cylinder to the master cylinder. Keep going until fluid rising out of the small hole in the bottom of the reservoir comes up clean and with no bubbles. Pull fluid out of the reservoir with a second syringe now and then so it does not overflow.
verification: Fluid from the reservoir hole is clean and bubble-free
Reservoir has not overflowed

steps.title: Close the slave bleeder
steps.instruction: Snug the slave bleeder while the syringe is still pressing, then remove the syringe and hose and refit the dust cap. Wipe off any fluid around the slave cylinder.
verification: Bleeder snug
Dust cap on
No fluid on the engine case

steps.title: Set the reservoir level
steps.instruction: With the reservoir still level, set the fluid 4 mm (0.16 in) below the reservoir rim. Fit the membrane and cover and tighten the screws. The level climbs as the clutch plates wear, so do not overfill.
verification: Fluid 4 mm below the rim
Cover fitted

steps.title: Check the clutch lever and disengagement
steps.instruction: Pull the clutch lever several times: it should feel the same every pull with a clear take-up point. Start the engine, pull the lever and select first; the bike should not creep or lurch. Wash off any spilled fluid with water.
verification: Lever feel consistent
Clutch disengages fully with the engine running
No spilled fluid left on the bike
